Process maps, state machines and exceptions

After this lesson you can:
  • Model actors, events and states separately
  • Specify guards and restrictive failure paths
  • Cover timeout, retry, cancellation and repair

Learning rhythm: read one section at a time, pause to explain the control in your own words, then answer the knowledge check without looking back.

On this page
  1. Three complementary views
  2. The transition table
  3. Exception completeness
  4. Regulatory anchors
  5. Where this lives in LoanOS
  6. Knowledge check

1. Three complementary views

A journey map shows actors and experience.

BPMN/swimlanes show responsibility and hand-off.

A state model defines legal states, triggering commands, guards and resulting events.

Use all three when hand-offs and system invariants matter.

2. The transition table

For each transition record source state, command, actor/authority, required facts/evidence, policy version, target state, emitted events and communication. Specify invalid-state response and idempotency key.

3. Exception completeness

Walk provider timeout, stale evidence, duplicate request, partial success, human referral, rejection, expiry, withdrawal, reversal, reconciliation break and operator repair. Fail closed and create owned work; never let an error become silent success.

Regulatory anchors

  • RBI-IT-GRC — Requirements, change and test evidence must support controlled, auditable processing.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.
